title: continue with AntiGravity and implement the missing Live Perc…
objective:
continue with AntiGravity and implement the missing Live Perception and Low-Latency Voice architecture. Do not create isolated hardcoded fixes for Comet or Camera. Build one reusable perception layer for every desktop application.
1. Browser live perception
When I ask things such as:
“What is on my Comet Perplexity page right now?”
“Read what is on my browser.”
“What do you see on my screen?”
“What page am I looking at?”
Jarvis must inspect the CURRENT foreground browser/window for THAT SAME TURN.
For Chromium-based browsers including Comet, prefer browser-native evidence when available:
- active window
- active tab
- URL
- title
- DOM/accessibility tree
- visible text
- current viewport screenshot
If browser-native access is unavailable, fall back to Windows window capture / desktop capture and visual perception of the actual foreground window.
Every observation must contain:
- goalRunId
- turnId
- HWND/window identity
- process
- capture timestamp
- URL/title when available
- screenshot/frame hash
- extracted visible content
Evidence from a previous turn must never answer a new perception request.
2. Desktop live perception
Build a universal observe_current_screen / observe_window capability.
Jarvis must be able to answer:
“What is on my desktop right now?”
“What do you see inside Hermes?”
“Read the Word window.”
“What is visible in Telegram?”
It should automatically identify the requested window, capture fresh visual evidence, combine UI Automation/accessibility information with screenshot vision, and answer from that evidence.
Do not answer from cached UI text, process existence, previous screenshots, or generic templates.
3. Camera live perception
When I say:
“Look at me.”
“What am I holding?”
“What do you see through the camera?”
“Describe what I am showing you.”
capture a NEW webcam frame for that exact turn and run visual perception on the frame.
Opening Camera.exe is NOT camera perception.
A successful camera-perception response requires:
- same-turn webcam frame
- timestamp
- dimensions
- frame hash
- vision result tied to that frame
If no fresh frame exists, Jarvis must say:
“I don’t currently have a fresh camera frame.”
Jarvis must never claim “I can see you” without fresh visual evidence.
For conversational continuity, optionally maintain a local short-lived camera ring buffer or low-rate local stream, but do not persist video unnecessarily. Current-turn evidence remains mandatory for claims about what I am doing or holding.
4. Fix turn isolation
Each microphone turn must have its own immutable:
- turnId
- goalRunId
- transcript
- intent
- action plan
- observation/evidence
- response
Previous camera, screenshot, browser, or application intents must never leak into the next request.
Conversational memory remains available, but EXECUTION STATE must be isolated per turn.
Fix STT/intent normalization for phrases such as:
- Comet Perplexity
- browser
- screen
- camera
- Hermes 1
- Zeus
A transcription error must not silently become an unrelated tool action.
5. Low-latency voice
Instrument the entire voice path:
microphone → Deepgram interim STT → endpoint detection → intent routing → tool/perception → LLM → first TTS sentence → audio playback
Record timestamps for every stage.
Implement:
- streaming STT
- semantic endpointing
- partial transcript processing
- deterministic fast routing for simple commands
- parallel capability preparation while the final transcript is stabilizing
- sentence/phrase-level streaming TTS
- immediate playback of sentence 1 while later sentences are still generating
- barge-in/interruption support
- playback completion tracking so final words are never clipped
Target normal conversational speech-end-to-first-audio at approximately 500–800 ms where the requested action does not itself require a slow external operation.
Report p50 and p95 latency separately.
6. No-response watchdog
Jarvis sometimes receives my speech but gives no answer.
Add a turn watchdog.
Every accepted voice turn must terminate in exactly one of:
- ANSWERED
- EXECUTING
- REPAIRING
- BLOCKED
- FAILED
Never silently disappear.
If processing exceeds about 2 seconds without a user-visible result, Jarvis should give a short truthful acknowledgment such as:
“I’m checking the active browser now.”
It must not invent completion.
7. Integrate with autonomous self-heal
These perception abilities must use the existing self-healing architecture.
If active-browser capture, desktop observation, camera capture, vision inference, voice playback, or verification fails:
failure → same GoalRun → AntiGravity repair → build → deploy → retry original request → Argus verification
I must not have to say “delegate this to AntiGravity.”
8. Acceptance tests must use my real Jarvis production path
Do not certify using only helper scripts.
After implementation, test the installed Agentic OS with these exact requests:
“Jarvis, tell me what is currently on my Comet Perplexity page.”
Jarvis must describe the CURRENT page and provide evidence from the active tab/window.
“Jarvis, what is on my desktop right now?”
Jarvis must capture and describe the current screen.
“Jarvis, what am I holding?”
A new webcam frame must be captured and the visible object described. Change the object and repeat; the answer must change according to the fresh frame.
“Jarvis, what is visible inside Hermes 1?”
Jarvis must inspect fresh current content.
Run ten consecutive conversational turns and prove there is no stale-intent leakage.
Measure speech latency over at least ten normal turns and report p50/p95.
Do not declare this task complete because the camera device exists, a browser process exists, or a screenshot file exists. Completion means Jarvis can perceive and discuss the CURRENT visual state conversationally through the normal installed voice experience. Continue until this is verified or there is a genuine external blocker.

Relevant Context:
Requested over the JARVIS live conversation channel.
